title: Western coast and interior · Summer
subtitle: Southern summer drying gives way to northern ocean weather and sheltered inland plains.
notes: 1 · Chardon and the southern basins: stable ridge, coastal fog and a summer moisture deficit.
2 · Western forests: winter recharge and shade bridge dry intervals; showers persist farther north.
3 · Fiatara and the plains: exposed mountains intercept moisture; sheltered grasslands receive intermittent rain.

title: Western coast and interior · Winter
subtitle: Ocean storms reach farther south; maritime thaws alternate with interior cold outbreaks.
notes: 1 · Chardon and Apporia: returning western storms replenish rivers and soils.
2 · Forests and high slopes: rain below, snow higher up; snow storage releases water during the thaw.
3 · Mawar and Fiatara: exposed storms and snowy high terrain; milder coastal intervals can interrupt winter cold.

title: Dunmar and the Nevos · Summer
subtitle: West to southwest inflow reaches the Darba saddle; terrain and moisture loss dry the interior.
notes: 1 · Broad Darba saddle: maritime monsoon air enters between the Chataan and Yuvanti systems.
2 · Dunmari progression: wetter west and north; variable onset, rain spells and breaks farther inland.
3 · Hara and Garamjala: shelter and depleted inflow preserve dryness; isolated storms are not a second wet climate.

title: Dunmar and the Nevos · Winter
subtitle: The monsoon withdraws; winter ocean weather reaches the Chataans from the west.
notes: 1 · Chataans and Alta Tonaro: western disturbances provide winter rain or high snow on suitable exposures.
2 · Dunmar: cooler continental flow and longer dry intervals; earlier rains continue to support water and vegetation.
3 · Nevos shores and islands: maritime moderation persists; Illoria has no assigned local rainfall calendar.

title: Sentinels and northern highlands · Summer
subtitle: Two maritime moisture sources meet a long mountain barrier; elevation limits the warm season.
notes: 1 · Western slopes: remaining ocean disturbances and stored snowmelt support exposed forests and headwaters.
2 · Eastern foothills: Green Sea moisture can generate upslope cloud and storms without wetting every interior basin.
3 · Southern high country: dry intervals and thaw contrast with persistent ice near the highest peaks.

title: Sentinels and northern highlands · Winter
subtitle: Wet western slopes border sheltered basins and continental cold; snow remains uneven across the range.
notes: 1 · Western snowfall: uplift favors exposed slopes; sheltered valleys receive less precipitation.
2 · Zimkova and Vostok: inland exposure and cold-air retention matter as well as elevation.
3 · Southern passes: episodic snow and drifting can close high routes despite a broadly dry mountain climate.

title: Southern mainland · Northern summer
subtitle: The tropical rain belt moves north while the subtropical desert remains broadly arid.
notes: 1 · Shrev–Nayan margin: maritime access and terrain allow tropical forest beside the drier plateau.
2 · Drankor and the mainland jungle coast: episodic coastal inflow supports humid heat and heavy rain; local timing is open.
3 · Great Desert: a heat low does not guarantee rain; limited supply and dry air above preserve interior aridity.
footer: Dashed purple arrows: illustrative maritime incursions. Orekatu is separate and is not located or assigned a calendar here.

title: Southern mainland · Northern winter
subtitle: The rain belt shifts south; coastal tropical moisture and dry interior conditions remain distinct.
notes: 1 · Northern tropical margins: longer dry intervals can develop as summer inflow retreats; forest moisture is stored.
2 · Drankor and the mainland jungle coast: episodic coastal inflow supports humid heat and heavy rain; local timing is open.
3 · Desert interior: cooler conditions and weaker summer heating do not establish a rainy winter.
footer: Dashed purple arrows: illustrative maritime incursions. Orekatu is separate and is not located or assigned a calendar here.

title: Sentinels · Winter storm redevelopment
subtitle: An illustrative episode: upper-air disturbance crosses the range; a low draws fresh eastern moisture inland.
notes: 1 · A disturbance can cross above the mountain barrier after low-level western air has lost much of its moisture.
2 · A low south of the heartlands draws Green Sea air westward on its northern side, producing rain or snow inland.
3 · Later development is favored farther offshore; the Western Gulf retains its relative shelter. Exact tracks remain open.
footer: Blue dashed arrows: illustrative disturbance / storm movement. Purple: surface air. This is an episode, not a seasonal mean.
